title: Capturing Lacunary Iron–Oxo Keggin Clusters and Insight Into the Keggin-Fe Cluster Rotational Isomerization

material_class.structural_family: Lanthanum-capped, dimeric lacunary β-Keggin iron–oxo cluster

synthesis.procedure: Obtained by reacting iron acetate and lanthanum perchlorate in the presence of a small amount of N-methyldiethanolamine. The main article refers to the Supporting Information for the preparation but gives no numerical reagent amount.

reagents.name: iron acetate
reagents.formula: Fe(OAc), as rendered in the article

reagents.name: N-methyldiethanolamine
reagents.amount: a small amount; no numerical quantity reported

reagents.name: sodium hydroxide aqueous solution
reagents.amount: freshly prepared 1.0 M; added dropwise until incipient but permanent precipitation

synthesis.time: 2 hours under reflux; crystals obtained after approximately two weeks
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered, then evaporated under ambient conditions to obtain reddish-brown cuboid crystals.

properties.summary: Compound 1 displays ferrimagnetic interaction; the main article points to Figure S2 without giving numerical magnetic measurements.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The La6Fe22 cation contains a sandwich-like Fe22 oxo core capped by six hydrated La3+ units. The Fe22 core consists of two face-to-face, bivacant β-Keggin Fe11 subclusters linked through oxygen coordination. The article further describes each Fe11 subcluster in terms of a trivacant β-Keggin Fe10 unit.

synthesis.procedure: Crystals can form when compound 1 is dissolved in water or an isopropanol–water mixture, albeit in very poor yield. The article states that a higher yield can be achieved by a reaction similar to that used for 1, with the pH adjusted to approximately 5.0; it provides no numerical reagent amount for that preparation.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The cation comprises an α-Keggin Fe13 oxo core capped on its six square faces by hydrated La3+ units. A central tetrahedrally coordinated Fe3+ lies within a cage of twelve octahedrally coordinated Fe3+ ions.
